name: Harim
overview: Harim is a male biblical figure known primarily as the father of Malchijah, as recorded in Nehemiah 3:11. There is no information about his tribal affiliation or additional notes. His mention is brief and focused on his paternal role.
namesAndTitles: The name Harim means 'consecrated [to YHWH],' indicating a dedication or setting apart to the Lord. This proper name is not indicated as given directly by God but carries a significant meaning reflecting a life devoted to God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Harim as the father of Malchijah, based on Nehemiah 3:11. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Harim's significance lies in his identification through his son Malchijah, who is listed among those involved in the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls. This association places Harim within the community committed to restoring the city and its worship life after the exile, highlighting a legacy of faithfulness in a critical period of Israel's history.
